# SCIM user lifecycle

When you enable SCIM, your identity provider (IdP) becomes the source of truth for user management, automatically synchronizing user creation, updates, and deactivation with <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name -->.

## Overview

SCIM lets enables your IdP automatically manage the complete user lifecycle:

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->

- When a new employee is assigned to the Terraform Enterprise application in your IdP, SCIM automatically creates their account. No manual account creation is required.
- When user attributes change in your IdP, such as email or username, SCIM synchronizes those changes to Terraform Enterprise in real-time.

<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->
<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->

- When a new employee is assigned to your organization, SCIM automatically creates their account. No manual account creation is required.
- When user attributes change in your IdP, such as email or username, SCIM synchronizes those changes to HCP Terraform in real-time.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name -->

- When an employee leaves or is removed from the application in your IdP, SCIM immediately revokes their access by suspending their account.

This automation eliminates manual user management overhead and ensures that terminated employees cannot retain access to the platform.

## User lifecycle operations

All operations use the `/scim/v2/Users` endpoint.

### Create user

When your IdP provisions a new user, <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> performs the following actions:

1. Creates a user record or links an existing user with the same email address.
1. Creates a SCIM identity record that links the user to your IdP.
1. Returns a unique SCIM `id` that your IdP uses for all subsequent operations on this user.

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:create-scim-user -->
By default, the new user has no team memberships or organization access. Team membership is managed separately through [SCIM group provisioning](/terraform/enterprise/scim/groups).
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:create-scim-user -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:create-scim-user -->
HCP Terraform adds new users to the organization automatically without requiring an invitation or email verification.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:create-scim-user -->

### Update user

When user attributes change in your IdP, <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> updates the corresponding user record. Supported updates include:

- Email address changes
- SCIM `userName` changes
- External ID changes
- Active status changes

Updates apply synchronously and take effect immediately. <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> supports the following `PATCH` behaviors for users:

- `Replace` on supported user attributes, either as a targeted operation with a `path` or without a `path` when `value` is an object.
- `Add` on single-valued supported user attributes, which <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> treats the same as `Replace`.
- `Remove` for `externalId`.

You must include the `path` to perform a `Remove` operation. <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> ignores attempts to clear required user attributes such as `userName`, `emails`, or `active`. 

### Deactivate user

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:deactivate-scim-user -->
When your IdP sets `active=false` for a user or removes them from the application, Terraform Enterprise suspends the user by setting a `suspended_at` timestamp. Suspended users:

- Cannot log in to Terraform Enterprise
- Retain their user record and historical data
- Can be reactivated if the IdP provisions them again with `active=true`

If the suspended user was a site administrator through SCIM, Terraform Enterprise revokes that administrative access when the user is suspended.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:deactivate-scim-user -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:deactive-scim-user -->
When your IdP sets `active=false` for a user or removes them from the organization, HCP Terraform removes the user from your organization. The behavior depends on how the user was created:

- For SCIM-managed user accounts, HCP Terraform deletes users that have been removed from the organization.
- For manually-managed users, HCP Terraform removes users from the organization but retains their accounts so that they can access other organizations.

You can reactivate users by provisioning them again in your IdP with `active=true`.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:deactive-scim-user -->

### Delete user

When your IdP sends a delete request, <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> performs the following actions:

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-delete-user -->
- Deletes the SCIM identity record that links the user to the IdP
- Suspends the Terraform Enterprise user record
- Revokes site administrator access if the user had it through SCIM

Terraform Enterprise does not delete the underlying user record through SCIM delete.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-delete-user -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-delete-user -->
- Deletes the SCIM identity record that links the user to the IdP
- Removes the user from the organization
- For SCIM-managed users, deletes the user account
- For manually-managed users, HCP Terraform removes them from the organization but preserves their account for access to other organizations
<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-delete-user -->

|----------------|---------------------------|-------------|
| `userName` | `scim_username` | The IdP-managed username stored with the SCIM identity. Must be unique across the <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-user-attr -->instance<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-user-attr --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-user-attr -->organization<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-user-attr -->. |
| `emails[primary=true].value` | `email` | The user's primary email address. Must be unique across the <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-user-attr -->instance<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-user-attr --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-user-attr -->organization<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-user-attr -->. |
| `active` | <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-user-attr -->`suspended_at`<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-user-attr --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-user-attr -->User status<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-user-attr --> | When `active=false`, <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-user-attr -->sets `suspended_at` to the current timestamp<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-user-attr --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-user-attr --> the user's status changes to `Inactive`<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-user-attr -->. When `active=true`, <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-user-attr -->clears `suspended_at`<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-user-attr --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-user-attr -->provisions or reactivates the user<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-user-attr -->. |

When creating the user record, the SCIM `userName` does not become the <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> username. Instead, <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> generates the internal <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> `username` value. <!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-user-attr -->HCP Terraform also uses the `userName` to attribute to automatically map users to their single sign-on `nameid`s. Refer to [Team Names and SSO Team ID](/terraform/cloud-docs/users-teams-organizations/single-sign-on#nameid-format) for more information.  <!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-user-attr -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-name-fields -->
Terraform Enterprise does not store SCIM name fields, such as `givenName`, `familyName`, `middleName`. These attributes are accepted in requests but not persisted.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-name-fields -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-name-fields -->
HCP Terraform does not store SCIM name fields, such as `givenName`, `familyName`, `middleName`. These attributes are accepted in requests but not persisted.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-name-fields -->

## Existing users

If an incoming SCIM user has the same email address as an existing system user, <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> links that existing user to SCIM management as long as the incoming `userName` is not already owned by a different SCIM identity.

After <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> creates the SCIM identity link, the IdP initiates any future updates to that user. <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> keeps a single underlying user record.

If <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> does not find a matching email address, it creates a new user record and generates the local `username` separately from the SCIM `userName`.

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-linked-users -->
Terraform Enterprise stores the original `userName` sent by the IdP in the `scim_username` field. This enables the IdP to query by its original username even when the Terraform Enterprise username differs.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-linked-users -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-linked-users -->
HCP Terraform stores the original `userName` sent by the IdP in the `scim_username` field. This enables the IdP to query by its original username even when the HCP Terraform username differs.

When an existing user's email address that has been linked to an IdP identity, you must use the HCP Terraform UI to update their email address. HCP Terraform rejects updates to the `emails[primary=true].value` attribute because it represents global objects that can be associated with multiple organizations. 
<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-linked-users -->


## SCIM-managed versus manually-managed users

Users in <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> are either SCIM-managed or manually-managed. The management type affects what operations are allowed.

### SCIM-managed users

A user is SCIM-managed if they have an associated SCIM identity record. You can identify SCIM-managed users through the following indicators<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-user-indicators --> in the HCP Terraform UI<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-user-indicators -->:

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-user-indicators -->
The following indicators appear on Terraform Enterprise JSON:API user responses, not on the public SCIM `/scim/v2/Users` response shape:

- Terraform Enterprise JSON:API user responses include `scim-username` and `scim-updated-at` attributes
- The user was created or linked through SCIM provisioning
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-user-indicators -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-user-indicators -->
- User status shows **Synced - Provisioned** for users created by SCIM
- User status shows **Synced - Claimed** for existing users linked to SCIM
- The user was created or linked through SCIM provisioning

The HCP Terraform UI refers to SCIM-managed users as **organization-owned** and refers to manually-managed users as **user-owned**.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-user-indicators -->

### Behavior when SCIM is enabled

Users provisioned through SCIM become SCIM-managed. Existing users that were created manually are manually-managed until provisioned through SCIM.

If an IdP provisions a user whose email matches an existing manual user, that user becomes SCIM-managed. You can still create manually-managed users directly for emergency access.

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-enabled-behavior -->
Existing users who are not provisioned with SCIM can still access the organization. However, HCP Terraform cannot add them to a SCIM managed team and removes them from any SCIM managed teams.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-enabled-behavior -->

### Transition from manual to SCIM management

When you enable SCIM, existing users are not automatically converted. A user becomes SCIM-managed only when the IdP creates the user through SCIM and when the IdP provisions a user whose email matches an existing user.

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-site-admin -->
## Site administrator provisioning

You can provision site administrators through SCIM using a designated SCIM group.

Configure the `site-admin-group-scim-id` setting in your SCIM configuration to specify which SCIM group Terraform Enterprise uses for site administrator provisioning. For the full site admin group behavior, refer to [Manage SCIM provisioning](/terraform/enterprise/scim/manage#site-admin-group-behavior).

When SCIM is enabled, site administrator provisioning through SAML attributes is disabled. You must manage site administrators using the configured site admin group.

For more information about site administrators, refer to [Site Administration Permissions](/terraform/enterprise/users-teams-organizations/users#site-admin-permissions).
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-site-admin -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-multi-org -->
### Multi-organization access

SCIM-managed users are scoped to a single organization. When logging in, they must specify the organization name. To access a different organization, they must log out and log in again with the other organization name.

Manually-managed users can access multiple organizations with a single login session. After logging in, they see a list of all organizations they are members of, including non-SSO organizations, SSO organizations, and organizations with SCIM enabled.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-multi-org -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-emergency-access -->
## Owners team and emergency access

You cannot manage membership of the owners team with SCIM. This ensures that accounts used for emergencies, also referred to as **break-glass** accounts, are available even when SCIM is misconfigured. This also provides access when IdP changes would otherwise prevent administrators from being able to access HCP Terraform. Users managed by SCIM don't have emergency access because they are scoped to the organization and deleted when removed from the IdP.

Although you can't manage owner membership through SCIM, you can still deprovision users on the owners team. If you need to use an owner account to remediate a potential issue, verify that the account is active in the IdP.  

HCP Terraform requires at least one manually-managed account in the owners team to ensure break-glass access in case of SCIM misconfiguration. Your IdP can still manage team membership for users that are manually managed in HCP Terraform. These users appear in the UI as  **Synced - Claimed**. Membership within the owners team, however, is outside of SCIM controls.

We recommend maintaining at least two manually-managed, accounts in the owners team for emergency access. 

To maintain emergency access when SSO or SCIM are misconfigured or your IdP is unavailable:

- Ensure account is SCIM active
- Maintain separate manually-managed accounts with password authentication
- Place these accounts in the owners team
- Limit the number of accounts in the owners team to minimize security risk
- Document break-glass procedures for your team
<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-emergency-access -->

## Blocked operations for SCIM-managed users

To maintain the IdP as the single source of truth, certain operations are blocked for SCIM-managed users. Administrators must make changes through the IdP rather than directly in the UI or API.

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-blocked-ops -->
### Account API

A note on surfaces: these are Terraform Enterprise JSON:API endpoints, not the public SCIM `/scim/v2/*` provisioning endpoints.

| Endpoint | Method | Blocked | Reason |
|----------|--------|---------|--------|
| `/api/v2/account/details` | `GET` | No | Read operations are always allowed. |
| `/api/v2/account/update` | `PATCH` | Yes (`403`) | Identity attributes are managed by SCIM. |
| `/api/v2/account/password` | `PATCH` | Yes (`403`) | Identity and access state are managed through SCIM and SSO configuration. |

### Users API

| Endpoint | Method | Blocked | Reason |
|----------|--------|---------|--------|
| `/api/v2/users/:user_id` | `GET` | No | Read operations are always allowed. |

### Admin UI actions

| Action | Blocked | Reason |
|--------|---------|--------|
| Suspend user | Yes | User lifecycle is managed by SCIM. |
| Anonymize user | Yes | User lifecycle is managed by SCIM. |
| Delete user | Yes | User lifecycle is managed by SCIM. |

<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-blocked-ops -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-blocked-ops -->
The following actions are blocked for SCIM-managed users and teams:

- Editing user profile information. Note that you can still edit profile information for non-SCIM users 
- Adding or removing users from teams.
- Deleting users or teams.

Your IdP controls profile fields, such as name and email, for SCIM-managed users. Update these fields in your IdP. HCP Terraform may overwrite changes made directly in the UI.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-blocked-ops -->

### Operations that remain available

SCIM controls the user identity attributes and whether the user is active, but it does not control how the user authenticates to APIs. Users can perform operations that control platform-specific functionality rather than identity<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-available-ops -->.<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-available-ops --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-available-ops -->, including:<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-available-ops -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-available-ops -->
Users can call [user token API endpoints](`/api/v2/users/:user_id/authentication-tokens`) to create, list, and revoke their own API tokens for programmatic access to Terraform Enterprise.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:scim-available-ops -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:scim-available-ops -->
- Creating, listing, and revoking their own API tokens for programmatic access
- Assigning team permissions to workspaces
- Managing workspace settings
- Creating and managing teams that are not managed by SCIM
- Managing organization settings
<!-- END: TFC:only name:scim-available-ops -->

## SAML and SCIM username

When SCIM is enabled, <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> stops synchronizing SCIM-managed user identity from SAML assertions. Updates to SCIM `userName` must come from the IdP through SCIM. This ensures that SCIM remains the single source of truth for SCIM-managed user identity attributes.

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->
HCP Terraform maps users to the SAML single sign-on `nameid` based on the SCIM `userName` object. Neither the `Username` SAML assertion nor the the SCIM `userName` affect the HCP Terraform `username` object.   

SCIM is authoritative for team membership. HCP Terraform ignores any membership information passed during SAML SSO login, even when it contains membership information for teams that are not managed by SCIM. This approach avoids conflicts and simplifies compliance auditing.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name -->
